title: US Charges Lawrence Bishnoi and Goldy Brar in Hardeep Singh Nijjar Murder Case; FBI Offers $50,000 Reward
summary: The United States Department of Justice has filed charges against Lawrence Bishnoi (currently imprisoned in India) and Goldy Brar for allegedly ordering and orchestrating the June 2023 murder of Canadian Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Surrey, British Columbia. The FBI has offered a $50,000 reward for information leading to Goldy Brar's arrest. The US indictment stops short of directly accusing the Indian government, but places these gangsters at the centre of a transnational murder conspiracy. The charges follow Canada's earlier accusations against India over the Nijjar killing, which had severely strained India-Canada diplomatic relations.
exam_angle: Critically relevant for GS Paper 2 (International Relations) — India-Canada diplomatic crisis, transnational organised crime, and India-US relations. Also tests understanding of extradition frameworks and Five Eyes intelligence sharing.
key_facts: Accused: Lawrence Bishnoi (jailed in India) and Goldy Brar
Victim: Hardeep Singh Nijjar, killed June 2023 in Surrey, Canada
Charged by: US Department of Justice
FBI reward: $50,000 for Goldy Brar's arrest

title: US-Iran Military Strikes Escalate; Trump Declares Ceasefire Deal 'Over', Oil Prices Surge
summary: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes, escalating tensions in the Middle East after a brief ceasefire attempt collapsed. President Donald Trump declared the ceasefire 'a waste of time' and 'over', signalling continued US military engagement. Following Trump's remarks, Brent crude oil prices surged 6.3% to $78.8 per barrel, reflecting global supply risk concerns. Four oil and gas tankers turned back from the Strait of Hormuz after vessel attacks, with Iran reportedly ordering ships to avoid the Omani corridor — a development with direct implications for India's energy security and oil imports.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (IR) — US foreign policy, Middle East geopolitics, and Strait of Hormuz as a chokepoint. Connects to GS Paper 3 (Energy Security) — India's dependence on Gulf oil imports and vulnerability to West Asian conflicts.
key_facts: US and Iran exchanged military strikes; Trump declared ceasefire 'over'
Brent crude rose 6.3% to $78.8 per barrel
Four oil/LNG tankers turned back from Strait of Hormuz
Iran ordered ships to avoid Omani corridor

title: PM Modi Visits Prambanan Temple, Unveils India-Indonesia Heritage Plaque; BrahMos Partnership Sealed
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the 1,000-year-old Prambanan Hindu temple complex in Indonesia during his state visit and unveiled a joint India-Indonesia heritage commemorative plaque, highlighting civilisational links between the two nations. Separately, India and Indonesia officially sealed a BrahMos supersonic cruise missile partnership, marking a significant defence export milestone for India. The BrahMos deal with Indonesia had been in negotiation since 2022 and represents India's growing defence export footprint in Southeast Asia.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) — India's Act East Policy, ASEAN relations, and defence diplomacy. The BrahMos export connects to GS Paper 3 (Defence/Sci-Tech) — indigenisation and defence exports under Atmanirbhar Bharat.
key_facts: PM Modi visited Prambanan temple (1,000-year-old Hindu temple, Indonesia) and unveiled India-Indonesia heritage plaque
India and Indonesia sealed BrahMos supersonic cruise missile partnership
BrahMos is a joint venture between India's DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya
Reflects India's Act East Policy and growing defence exports

title: PM Modi's Australia Visit: 'Rock Star' Welcome Amid Human Rights Protests
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Australia as part of his multi-nation tour, receiving a large-scale welcome from the Indian diaspora described as a 'rock star' reception. The visit also witnessed human rights protests related to the Khalistan issue and the Nijjar murder case. Modi's Australia visit is part of broader efforts to strengthen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and Australia, which covers trade, defence, education, and critical minerals.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) — India-Australia bilateral relations, Quad grouping, and diaspora diplomacy. Context of the Nijjar case protests adds a layer connecting to India-Canada-Australia diplomatic tensions.
key_facts: PM Modi visited Australia as part of multi-nation tour
India-Australia relationship status: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
Australia is a member of the Quad alongside India, USA, and Japan
Visit coincided with human rights protests over Khalistan issue and Nijjar case

title: Sensex Sinks 1,680 Points, Nifty Closes Below 23,900 Amid US-Iran Escalation and Global Uncertainty
summary: Indian equity markets witnessed a sharp selloff on July 8, 2026, with the BSE Sensex falling approximately 1,680 points and Nifty50 closing below 23,900, a drop of nearly 2%. The primary triggers were Trump's declaration that the US-Iran ceasefire was 'over', rising crude oil prices, and broader global risk-off sentiment. The market crash affected energy, banking, and aviation stocks most severely. This reflects the high sensitivity of Indian markets to geopolitical developments in the Middle East given India's oil import dependence.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy) — transmission of global geopolitical shocks to Indian financial markets, imported inflation via crude oil, and India's current account vulnerability.
key_facts: Sensex fell ~1,680 points on July 8, 2026
Nifty50 closed below 23,900 (approx. 2% decline)
Key trigger: US-Iran military escalation and rising crude oil prices
Brent crude rose 6.3% to $78.8/barrel on the same day
source: The Economic Times / The Times of India

title: Russia's Share in India's Oil Imports Crosses 40% in May 2026
summary: Russia's share in India's total crude oil imports crossed 40% in May 2026, maintaining its position as India's largest oil supplier even as Indian refiners continue to pay a premium over benchmark prices. This trend, which began after Western sanctions on Russia following the Ukraine invasion in 2022, has reshaped India's oil import basket significantly. The development is occurring against the backdrop of fresh geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, making India's energy diversification strategy critical.
exam_angle: Important for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy Security) — India's strategic oil sourcing, impact of sanctions on global energy markets, and India's balancing act between Western allies and Russia in energy trade.
key_facts: Russia's share in India's crude oil imports: >40% in May 2026
Russia is India's largest single crude oil supplier
India continues to pay a premium over benchmark prices for Russian oil
Shift began post-2022 Ukraine invasion and Western sanctions on Russia

title: India Urges US to Reconsider Proposed 12.5% Tariff Under USTR Section 301 'Forced Labour' Probe
summary: India has formally urged the United States to reconsider a proposed 12.5% additional tariff on Indian goods being considered under USTR's (United States Trade Representative) Section 301 investigation into alleged 'forced labour' practices. This comes amid already stalled India-US bilateral trade deal negotiations. The Section 301 mechanism allows the US to impose trade sanctions in response to practices it deems 'unreasonable or discriminatory'. India's goods exports to the US could be significantly impacted if the tariff is implemented.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy) — India-US trade relations, WTO-compatible trade remedy mechanisms, and the broader context of Trump-era tariff policies affecting Indian exports.
key_facts: US proposed 12.5% tariff on Indian goods under USTR Section 301
Reason cited: 'Forced labour' practices
India has formally requested reconsideration
Section 301 of US Trade Act allows unilateral tariffs on 'unfair' trade practices

title: India-US Trade Deal Remains Stuck Despite Diplomatic Engagement
summary: The much-awaited India-US bilateral trade agreement continues to remain stalled, with analysts citing multiple sticking points including US demands on market access for agricultural and dairy products, digital trade norms, and India's data localisation requirements. The ongoing tariff threats under USTR probes have further complicated negotiations. India is the US's largest trading partner in South Asia, and both sides had signalled intent to fast-track a deal.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy) — India-US trade architecture, protectionism versus liberalisation debate, and India's multilateral and bilateral trade strategy.
key_facts: India-US bilateral trade deal negotiations remain deadlocked
Key sticking points: agricultural market access, digital trade, data localisation
India is US's largest South Asian trading partner
Concurrent USTR tariff threats have complicated the negotiations

title: RBI and Tax Department Back Cryptocurrency Ban; Warn of Tax Evasion Risks
summary: Documents reviewed by Reuters reveal that India's central bank (RBI) has backed a blanket ban on cryptocurrencies, while the Income Tax Department has separately warned of significant tax evasion risks posed by crypto assets. The RBI's position reflects concerns about financial stability, monetary policy transmission, and capital flight. India currently taxes crypto gains at 30% with a 1% TDS on transactions, but regulatory clarity on the legal status of cryptocurrencies remains pending.
exam_angle: Important for GS Paper 3 (Economy) — RBI's monetary policy powers, cryptocurrency regulation debate in India, and digital asset governance. Links to the Cryptocurrency and Regulation of Official Digital Currency Bill.
key_facts: RBI has backed a blanket ban on cryptocurrencies
Income Tax Department warns of tax evasion through crypto
India currently taxes crypto gains at 30% + 1% TDS on transactions
Legal/regulatory status of crypto in India remains unresolved

title: Ethanol-Blend Fuel Backlash Intensifies in India; Carmakers Under Scrutiny
summary: A growing backlash against ethanol-blended fuel (particularly E20 — 20% ethanol blend) is intensifying in India, with consumer complaints about reduced engine performance and mileage, and carmakers facing criticism over inadequate adaptation of vehicle technology. India's National Policy on Biofuels targets 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025-26 under the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana and the Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP). The controversy raises questions about the pace of implementation versus vehicle fleet readiness.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Environment/Economy) — India's ethanol blending programme, biofuel policy, energy security, and the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana. Also links to reducing import dependence on crude oil.
key_facts: India targets 20% ethanol blending in petrol (E20) by 2025-26
Policy instrument: Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) and PM JI-VAN Yojana
Consumer backlash: complaints of reduced engine performance and mileage
Carmakers face scrutiny over inadequate adaptation to E20 fuel standards

title: Wayanad Debris Slip: 5 Missing, Amit Shah Pledges Centre's Support; Environmentalists Demand Halt to Tunnel Works
summary: A fresh debris slip in Wayanad district of Kerala left 5 persons missing, prompting Union Home Minister Amit Shah to pledge full central government support for rescue and relief operations. Environmental groups held the Kerala government accountable and demanded suspension of ongoing tunnel construction works in the ecologically sensitive Western Ghats region. Wayanad has witnessed repeated landslides and debris flows, underscoring the persistent vulnerability of the region to geological hazards, especially during the southwest monsoon season.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 3 (Environment/Disaster Management) — landslide vulnerability in Western Ghats, NDMA guidelines, and the broader debate over development versus environmental conservation in ecologically sensitive zones (ESZs).
key_facts: Location: Wayanad district, Kerala (Western Ghats)
Persons missing after debris slip: 5
Union Home Minister Amit Shah pledged Centre's support
Environmentalists demanded suspension of tunnel construction in the region

title: Supreme Court Questions Centre Over Blanket Ban on Pregnant IPS Officers During Probation Training
summary: The Supreme Court of India questioned the Union Government over a policy that imposes a blanket ban on pregnant IPS (Indian Police Service) officers from undergoing probation training, effectively stalling their career progression. The Court raised concerns that such a policy may violate the constitutional rights of women officers under Articles 14 (equality), 16 (equal opportunity in public employment), and 21 (right to life and personal liberty). The case raises significant questions about gender discrimination in India's civil services training framework.
exam_angle: Directly relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) — fundamental rights (Articles 14, 16, 21), gender equality in civil services, and judicial review of executive policies. Also connects to the Maternity Benefit Act and gender-sensitive governance.
key_facts: Issue: Blanket ban on pregnant IPS officers during probation training
Supreme Court questioned the Union Government on the policy
Constitutional provisions at stake: Articles 14, 16, and 21
IPS is an All India Service governed by the IPS (Cadre) Rules

title: Bombay High Court Upholds Woman's Right to Flee Forced Marriage; Invokes Personal Liberty
summary: The Bombay High Court protected a woman fleeing a forced marriage, invoking Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) and declaring 'Your Life, Your Choice'. The court refused to allow the woman to be returned to her matrimonial home against her will, affirming that individual autonomy and freedom from coercion are fundamental rights under the Constitution. The ruling reinforces a growing body of High Court jurisprudence protecting women's agency in matrimonial matters.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (Polity) — judicial interpretation of Article 21, fundamental rights, and the right to personal liberty. Connects to gender justice, habeas corpus petitions, and the expanding scope of the right to life.
key_facts: Court: Bombay High Court
Constitutional basis: Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty)
Ruling: Court protected woman fleeing forced marriage
Key phrase used by court: 'Your Life, Your Choice'

title: Ram Temple Donation Theft: SIT Report Names Avinash Shukla as Prime Accused; Security Lapses Identified
summary: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) report on theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has named Avinash Shukla as the prime accused. The SIT found that temple staff stole cash from donation boxes and that security protocols were not enforced. The report highlights systemic failures in the administration of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, which was consecrated in January 2024. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust manages the temple complex.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Governance) — accountability mechanisms in autonomous trusts, management of religious institutions, and the role of SITs in criminal investigation. The Ram Temple is a landmark institution under a government-formed trust.
key_facts: SIT named Avinash Shukla as prime accused in Ram Temple donation theft
SIT found: staff stole cash, security protocols not enforced
Managing body: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust
Ram Temple was consecrated in January 2024 in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh

title: NATO Summit: Trump Attacks Spain as 'Terrible Partner', Demands Greenland; Exposes Alliance Cracks
summary: At the NATO summit, US President Donald Trump launched a sharp attack on Spain, calling it 'a terrible partner' and threatening to cut off trade, labelling it 'a wasted cause'. Trump simultaneously reiterated demands for control over Greenland, citing its strategic importance for US defence and resource interests amid competition with Russia and China. The summit exposed significant internal divisions within NATO, with Trump questioning the value of collective defence commitments for allies he deems insufficiently compliant.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) — NATO's internal cohesion, US foreign policy under Trump, and Greenland's strategic importance. Connects to Arctic geopolitics and the shifting nature of multilateral alliances.
key_facts: Trump called Spain 'a terrible partner' and threatened trade cutoff at NATO summit
Trump reiterated demand for control over Greenland
Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark, strategically located in the Arctic
Summit exposed cracks in NATO's internal unity
source: The Times of India / Al Jazeera

title: Google to Expand AI Data Centres in India; Signals Growing Digital Infrastructure Investment
summary: Google's cloud business CEO Thomas Kurian announced that Google will set up more Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centres in India as demand for cloud and AI services grows. This is part of Google's broader global strategy to build AI infrastructure and aligns with India's Digital India and emerging data centre policy framework. The move follows similar announcements by other global tech giants and comes amid India's push to become an AI hub under the IndiaAI Mission.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Economy) — India's digital infrastructure development, IndiaAI Mission, data localisation debate, and India's emergence as a global AI hub. Connects to the National Data Governance Framework.
key_facts: Google to expand AI data centres in India; announced by Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian
India is targeting becoming a global AI hub under the IndiaAI Mission
Government of India has a dedicated Digital India programme and National Data Governance Framework
Reflects growing FDI in India's digital infrastructure sector

title: China Considering Restrictions on Overseas Access to Advanced AI Models
summary: China is reportedly weighing curbs on overseas access to its advanced Artificial Intelligence models, a move that could further fragment the global AI ecosystem and accelerate the AI technology decoupling between China and Western nations. This development comes amid US restrictions on export of advanced semiconductors to China and growing competition between the two nations in AI development. A global report also warned that AI firms worldwide are lagging on safety measures.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) and GS Paper 2 (IR) — AI governance, technology decoupling between US and China, global AI safety norms, and implications for India's AI strategy and tech diplomacy.
key_facts: China considering restricting overseas access to its advanced AI models
Context: Ongoing US-China technology decoupling, US semiconductor export controls
Separate global report warns AI firms worldwide are lagging on safety measures
Impacts global AI governance architecture and India's tech partnerships

title: Uttar Pradesh Approves Startup Policy 2026 with Focus on $1 Trillion Economy Target
summary: The Uttar Pradesh government under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath cleared the Startup Policy 2026, aimed at fostering entrepreneurship and innovation in the state with an eye on achieving UP's $1 trillion (₹84 lakh crore) economy goal. The policy is expected to provide incentives including seed funding, incubation support, and regulatory ease for startups. Uttar Pradesh has been aggressively positioning itself as an investment destination following successive Investor Summits.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy) and GS Paper 2 (Governance) — state-level startup ecosystems, economic decentralisation, and the connection between innovation policy and GDP targets. Connects to the national Startup India initiative.
key_facts: Policy: Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy 2026
Approved by: Yogi Adityanath-led UP government
Target: Support UP's $1 trillion economy goal
Key features: Seed funding, incubation support, regulatory ease

title: Lashkar-e-Taiba Commander Killed in Shopian Encounter, J&K
summary: A Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander who had been trapped in South Kashmir's Shopian district for four days was killed in a security forces encounter. Police confirmed the elimination of the LeT militant, with a search operation continuing for a second militant. The operation is part of ongoing counter-insurgency efforts by the Indian Army, CRPF, and J&K Police in the Kashmir Valley, where LeT remains one of the most active Pakistan-based terrorist organisations.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Internal Security) — counter-terrorism operations in J&K, Lashkar-e-Taiba's operational presence, and the role of unified command structure in J&K security operations.
key_facts: Outfit: Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), a Pakistan-based terrorist organisation
Location: Shopian district, South Kashmir
LeT commander killed after 4-day siege/encounter operation
Operation involved: Indian Army, J&K Police (unified command)

title: PM Modi Visits 1,000-Year-Old Prambanan Temple in Indonesia: Cultural Diplomacy and Heritage Linkages
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Prambanan temple complex in Yogyakarta, Indonesia — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest Hindu temple complexes in Southeast Asia, dating back to the 9th-10th century CE. Modi unveiled a joint India-Indonesia heritage plaque, emphasising the deep cultural and civilisational links between the two nations rooted in Hinduism, Sanskrit literature, and the Ramayana tradition. The visit underlines India's use of cultural diplomacy as a tool of soft power in the Indo-Pacific region.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 1 (Culture) — India's cultural links with Southeast Asia, Hindu temple architecture abroad, and UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Also connects to GS Paper 2 (IR) — India's soft power diplomacy and cultural outreach.
key_facts: Prambanan: UNESCO World Heritage Site, located in Yogyakarta, Indonesia
Age: ~1,000 years (built circa 9th-10th century CE), dedicated to the Hindu Trimurti
PM Modi unveiled India-Indonesia joint heritage plaque during visit
Prambanan reflects Hindu-Buddhist cultural influence in Southeast Asia (Indianisation)
